- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.20), model underestimates; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing downside risk.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes; apply a “cool-down” rule: cap forecast 3–5 days after spike at 10–15% below peak.
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 10+ consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a “lag correction”: reduce first 5–7 days by 5–10% to align with observed lagged behavior.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; match forecast direction to sentiment trend, not just magnitude.
